id: -560-阿契美尼德對科爾基斯的戰爭
theater: 黑海東岸法希斯河下游

battle.name: 阿契美尼德對科爾基斯的戰爭
battle.theater: 黑海東岸法希斯河下游
battle.brief: 公元前560年前後，阿契美尼德王權沿高加索通道向黑海東岸推進，壓服以法希斯河下游艾亞為中心的科爾基斯王國。帝國的混合兵種與科爾基斯重步兵所持的青銅包尖長矛同出一系，卡面的斯巴達長矛正是這類兩米長刺槍的典型。戰後科爾基斯被列為帝國西界的貢賦區，御道驛站接入其境內。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場衝突發生在阿契美尼德帝國王權向黑海東岸推進的關鍵年代，公元前560年前後。帝國一方並非單一常備軍，而是以各省總督轄下徵發的守備兵為骨架：波斯步兵（spāh）、王室近衛性質的「不死軍」（spāh vaš-spāh）、薩卡弓手與索格底亞弓手、持柳條盾的「持盾兵」（sparabara），加上各王的戰車與重騎，交由國王本人與分派的總指揮官分層統率；希臘語史料把這套監察體系稱為「國王的眼」。科爾基斯一方是黑海東岸的獨立王國，首都通常定在法希斯河下游的艾亞（埃祖格巴）一帶，另有第俄斯庫里亞斯、皮圖斯兩個靠海據點與若干希臘移民商鎮；王國以本地部落兵為主力，同時吸納沿海的希臘商人與傭兵。帝國在後方還得應付高加索山脈另一側的斯基提亞遊牧集團與米底舊勢力的壓力，因此這場戰爭既是一次邊境整固，也是一條糧道與商道的清理行動。
countriesEn: This clash came at the decisive moment when Achaemenid kingship was pushing toward the eastern shore of the Black Sea, around 560 BC. The imperial side was not a single standing army but a skeleton of levies raised by the satraps: Persian infantry (spāh), an elite household guard of the Immortals (spāh vaš-spāh), Sagartian and Sogdian archers, and the shield-bearing sparabara with wicker shields, together with the chariots and heavy cavalry of the kings, all commanded in layers by the Great King and the commanders he appointed; Greek sources call the supervising system the Eye of the King. Colchis was an independent kingdom on the eastern Black Sea, its capital usually placed at Aia (Ezugba) near the mouth of the Phasis, with the coastal bases of Dioscurias and Pityus and a number of Greek trading settlements beside them; the kingdom fielded local tribal levies as its main strength while absorbing Greek traders and mercenaries from the coast. Behind the imperial line the court still had to answer the pressure of the Scythian pastoral groups beyond the Caucasus and of the residual Median power, so this war was at once a consolidation of the frontier and a clearing of the grain road and the trade route.
people: 阿契美尼德一方最關鍵的人物是達里一世：他即位之後重整行省制度，把高加索—黑海走廊納入御道與財庫的統一調度，這類遠征才有可能成行。帝國的指揮層多由總督與王室近臣組成，貝希敦銘文所記載的對外用兵正反映這套以王為中心的指揮鏈條。科爾基斯一方的國王姓名在同期銘文中並無保存，後世希臘傳統卻以埃厄忒斯（Aeëtes，阿耳戈英雄傳說中的國王、美狄亞之父）稱呼他；科爾基斯王室的考古痕跡（公元前六世紀的貴族高塚墓葬）顯示，其統治者穿戴的是中亞—伊朗式樣的禮服並隨葬金器。希臘方面，米利都等城的移民在法希斯與第俄斯庫里亞斯建立商站，同時向帝國與科爾基斯雙方供應傭兵，而僱傭重裝步兵的營長正是希臘人最常出任的職位。希羅多德留下的最生動片段，是達里一世西征斯基提亞時科爾基斯人自願歸順並為大軍引路，兵力達數萬之眾，而且是唯一攜帶青銅包尖長矛的西方兵種——這段記載是本場戰爭唯一還能看見矛的原始線索。
peopleEn: The decisive figure on the Achaemenid side was Darius I: after taking the throne he reorganised the satrapies and folded the Caucasus–Black Sea corridor into the unified management of the Royal Road and the treasuries, and only that made a campaign of this kind feasible. The imperial command echelon was composed of satraps and royal courtiers, and the foreign campaigns recorded in the Behistun inscription reflect precisely this king-centred chain of command. The name of the Colchian king is not preserved in any contemporary inscription, though later Greek tradition calls him Aeëtes, the king of the Argonaut legend and father of Medea; the archaeological trace of the Colchian court, in the aristocratic kurgan burials of the sixth century BC, shows rulers dressed in Median-Iranian fashion and buried with gold vessels. On the Greek side, settlers from Miletus and other cities ran the emporia at Phasis and Dioscurias and sold mercenary service to both the empire and Colchis, and the commander of a hired hoplite contingent was the post most often held by Greeks. The most vivid surviving fragment comes from Herodotus: when Darius campaigned against the Scythians, the Colchians alone submitted of their own accord and guided the great army, a force of tens of thousands, and they were the only western contingent whose spears carried bronze tips. That passage is the one original trace that still lets us see a spear in this war.
kits: 卡面上的斯巴達長矛（dory）在此扮演的是同期技術譜系的代表，而不是戰場上直接採購的具名單件：兩米上下的木杆、前端葉形矛頭、槍尾銅套，正是愛琴海與希臘大陸重裝步兵的標準配備。科爾基斯自己的重步兵，據希羅多德描述，配的正是銅包尖長矛，裝備風格與密西安及呂基亞人相近，也就是說兩軍的矛兵在技術上彼此熟悉。希臘移民與傭兵在帝國軍中擔任方陣角色時，用 dory 配圓盾（aspis）構成密集的矛牆，常被編在軍陣側翼，掩護正面的弓陣。帝國的標準配置則是持盾兵（柳條 gerron 盾配短矛）、披皮甲或鱗甲的重裝弓手，以及大量不披甲、使用複合反曲弓的輕裝弓手，另有王族與總督的戰車隊和重甲騎兵。攻城方面有撞槌、攻城塔與土木作業，後世希臘戰術家埃涅阿斯·塔提庫斯留下的守城與攻城器械圖式，可與阿契美尼德時期的黑海作戰互相對照。運輸靠馱馬、驢車與御道驛站維持，海路則由愛奧尼亞水手操縱的內河與黑海船隊承擔。
kitsEn: The Spartan dory on this card stands for the technical family of the period rather than a named item taken straight from a battlefield: a shaft about two metres long, a leaf-shaped head and a bronze butt-spike, exactly the standard arm of the hoplite across the Aegean and the Greek mainland. Colchian heavy infantry, according to Herodotus, carried bronze-tipped spears of a type close to the Mysian and Lycian equipment, which means the spearmen of the two armies knew each other's technology on the field. When Greek settlers and mercenaries took their place inside the imperial order, they formed dory-and-aspis hoplite blocks, usually posted to the flanks to cover the front of the line. The imperial standard issue, by contrast, was the wicker-gerron shield-bearer with a short spear, armoured bowmen in scale or padded protection, and a large body of unarmoured light archers using composite recurve bows, alongside the chariot corps of the king and the satraps and the armoured cavalry. Siege work included rams, siege towers and earthworks, and the siege diagrams left by the Greek tactician Aeneas Tacticus can be compared with Achaemenid operations on the Black Sea. Supply was carried by pack animals, mule carts and relay stations on the Royal Road, while river and Black Sea transport was handled by Ionian crews.
tactics: 由於雙方的戰鬥記錄殘缺，戰術只能由三條可靠線索重構：一是地形，二是帝國軍固定的戰鬥程式，三是科爾基斯的地形特質。行動多在春季展開，隊伍沿安納托利亞與亞美尼亞方向北上，穿過高加索山脈的達里亞爾山口降到北坡，再順河谷向海岸推進。科爾基斯森林極密、降雨充沛、河川縱橫，重騎與戰車在這樣的林地與泥濘中難以展開，這正是帝國在西線避免讓波斯重騎單獨深入的原因。作戰程式是標準的混合兵種：先以密集弓陣齊射削弱敵陣，再由持盾兵與矛兵（希臘傭兵則是 dory 方陣）頂上，戰車與重騎在兩翼或敵陣側後衝擊，最後由攻城部隊處理城垣。守方倚賴地形：高地上的寨壘、木柵與居高臨下的拋射，迫使進攻方先做圍城與土木作業；攻城方則以圍城、斷糧、分兵離開主隊打游擊的方式拖延。海路提供另一條戰線：沿黑海與法希斯河的船隊可以繞過山道，把糧秣與攻城器械直接送到河口。
tacticsEn: Because the fighting itself is not recorded, tactics can only be reconstructed from three solid clues: the terrain, the fixed battle procedure of the imperial army, and the physical character of Colchis. Campaigns opened in spring; a column moved north from Anatolia and Armenia, crossed the Caucasus at the Darial pass, came down onto the northern slope and then followed the river valleys toward the coast. Colchis was extremely heavily wooded, with heavy rainfall and a mesh of rivers, and mounted troops and chariots could hardly manoeuvre in such ground and mud, which is why the empire avoided sending Persian heavy cavalry alone into the west. The pattern of battle was standard combined arms: massed archers opened with volleys to soften the enemy, shield-bearers and spearmen (dory blocks where Greek mercenaries served) pressed forward, chariots and heavy cavalry struck the flanks or the rear, and siege troops finished off fortified places. The defenders relied on the ground: hilltop strongholds, wooden palisades and plunging missiles forced the attacker into blockade and earthworks, while the besiegers replied with encirclement, cutting supplies and sending detachments out to raid and delay. The sea offered a second line of operations: ships on the Black Sea and the Phasis could bypass the mountain tracks and bring grain and siege equipment straight to the river mouth.
data: 關於這場戰爭的兵力與損失，史料幾乎完全沉默，這一點必須先講清楚。可以確定的數字有以下幾組。其一，希羅多德記載達里一世在公元前513年西征斯基提亞時集結了約七十萬步兵，若連隨軍人員則近百萬，他自己對這個數字持保留態度；這可以當作阿契美尼德帝國一次大規模西向動員的量級上限，而不是本役的實數。其二，同一部書記科爾基斯人在那支大軍中擔任引路與側翼任務，說明科爾基斯在帝國軍事編制裡是一支成建制的軍隊，而非零散徵發。其三，御道系統的可量化指標：從薩迪斯到蘇薩約三千帕拉桑加、一百一十一站，信使接力約七日走完全程（希羅多德書五），這決定了遠征軍的補給節奏與公文往返時間。其四，武器尺度：dory 全長約兩米，槍尾銅套是支撐與近身格鬥用的配重；科爾基斯平原與高加索西南麓出土的公元前六世紀高塚墓葬數十座，隨葬器物中可見中亞式金銀器與兵器配件，反映帝國式樣已隨軍隊與使團深入。其五，地理尺度：法希斯河（拉奧尼河）全長約三百三十公里，構成黑海東岸的交通與灌溉骨架；達里亞爾山口海拔約一千四百公尺，是橫越山脊的通道。關於雙方死傷數字，沒有任何可核的記載，此處不作推測。
dataEn: On the numbers of men and losses the historical record is almost silent, and that has to be said first. The following figures can be relied on. First, Herodotus reports that Darius I mustered about seven hundred thousand infantry for the Scythian campaign of 513 BC, close to a million if camp followers are counted, and he himself expresses doubt about the figure; it should be read as an upper bound on the scale of a major Achaemenid western mobilisation, not as an actual count for this war. Second, the same book assigns the Colchians a guiding and flanking role in that army, which shows that Colchis entered the imperial military order as an organised contingent rather than as ad hoc levies. Third, the quantifiable markers of the Royal Road: about three thousand parasangs and a hundred and eleven stations between Sardis and Susa, with the relay courier covering the whole route in roughly seven days (Herodotus, book V), which set the pace of resupply and of the exchange of dispatches for any distant army. Fourth, the scale of the weapon: the dory is about two metres long overall, and its bronze butt-spike served as a support and a weight in close fighting; the Colchian plain and the southwestern Caucasus have yielded several dozen sixth-century BC kurgan burials whose grave goods include Median-style gold and silver plate and weapon fittings, showing that imperial styles travelled inward with the armies and the embassies. Fifth, geography: the Phasis (the Rioni) runs some three hundred and thirty kilometres and forms the transport and irrigation backbone of the eastern shore, while the Darial pass sits at about fourteen hundred metres and forms the spine route of the range. No verifiable figures exist for casualties on either side, and no estimate is offered here.
cause: 開戰的理由是多層的，並非單一事件觸發。第一是地理與戰略：科爾基斯扼住黑海東岸，控制法希斯河下游的交通、金屬與木材資源，是阿契美尼德王權向黑海與高加索縱深延伸時繞不開的一段。帝國的西向邊界若止於小亞細亞與亞美尼亞，高加索山脈的另一側就長期敞開；把科爾基斯收編，等於同時解決北面的斯基提亞壓力與西線的商路。第二是財政：被征服的王朝按帝國制度轉為貢賦區，向波斯廷按年繳納白銀、穀物、牲畜與工藝品，這是帝國機器的燃料。第三是文明的吸引與互動：科爾基斯在希臘世界有「金羊毛」與阿耳戈英雄的傳說，是黑海最古老、也最有名的對外形象；米利都等城的希臘移民在法希斯與第俄斯庫里亞斯建立的商站，使這一地區很早就進入地中海的交換網絡。第四是制度的必然：御道、財庫與總督制一旦運轉，就要求把邊地變成可以被調度、被清點、被徵發的對象。當地王權是否真的拒絕進貢，是這場衝突的直接導火線，但相關細節沒有留下可靠記載。
causeEn: The reasons for the war were layered rather than triggered by a single incident. First, geography and strategy: Colchis held the eastern Black Sea, controlling the traffic of the lower Phasis along with its metal and timber resources, and it was a stretch the Achaemenid state could not bypass while extending toward the Black Sea and the Caucasian interior. If the empire's western frontier stopped in Anatolia and Armenia, the far side of the Caucasus stayed permanently open, and bringing Colchis in resolved the northern pressure from the Scythians and the western trade route at the same time. Second, finance: a conquered dynasty became a tribute district of the imperial system and paid the court in silver, grain, livestock and craft work every year, the fuel of the imperial machine. Third, attraction and exchange: in the Greek world Colchis carried the fame of the Golden Fleece and the Argonauts, the best known face of the Black Sea, and the emporia founded by Milesians and other cities at Phasis and Dioscurias had already pulled the region into the Mediterranean exchange network. Fourth, administrative inevitability: once the Royal Road, the treasuries and the satrapies were running, the frontier had to be turned into something that could be moved, counted and levied. Whether the local kings actually refused tribute was the immediate trigger, but no reliable account of that exchange survives.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是科爾基斯從獨立的黑海王國，變成阿契美尼德秩序中受帝國管轄的地區。史證上的痕跡相當一致：波斯波利斯的財庫與要塞檔案中出現「科爾基斯」這個受管區的名目，附有園丁、工役與徵發名冊，並有通往黑海東岸的御道驛站；考古上，公元前六世紀科爾基斯平原與高加索西南麓出現帶中亞—伊朗風格陪葬品的高塚墓葬，包括著名的阿哈爾戈里窖藏（金器、銀器與格里芬式造型），在物質層面把當地貴族與帝國中心的關係固定下來。錢幣是最硬的證據：科爾基斯在受波斯統治前後鑄造的銀質四德拉克馬（tetrobol），一面是戴人首的牛、一面是雙尾獅，中央有方形壓印，是黑海東岸最早成體系的本地造幣之一，說明這片土地在帝國框架內反而獲得了獨立的財政工具。希臘方面，戰後的黑海航線更安全，希臘商站與傭兵在帝國軍中的位置更穩，阿耳戈英雄「尋金羊毛」的傳說也在隨後兩三個世紀裡被希臘文人系統整理定型。長期看，帝國把高加索—黑海這條邊界釘住，但也把此地的希臘色彩、希臘商業與本地王權的殘餘一起保留下來，成為後來羅馬人接手時「科爾基斯王國」仍然存在的原因。
impactEn: The direct outcome was that Colchis passed from an independent Black Sea kingdom to an administered district inside the Achaemenid order. The documentary trace is consistent: the Persepolis fortification and treasury archives carry an entry for Colchis with lists of gardeners, labour and levies, and relay stations of the Royal Road reached the eastern shore; archaeologically, the sixth-century BC plains of Colchis and the southwestern Caucasus show elite kurgan burials with Median-Iranian grave goods, among them the famous Akhalgori treasure with its gold, silver and griffin-form vessels, fixing the relationship of the local aristocracy to the imperial centre in material form. Coinage is the hardest evidence: the Colchian silver tetrobol, struck in the region around the time of Persian rule, shows a man-headed bull on one face and a two-tailed lion on the other with a square incuse, and is one of the earliest locally coherent monetary issues on the eastern Black Sea, meaning the region obtained its own fiscal instrument inside the imperial framework. On the Greek side the Black Sea routes became safer, the position of the Greek emporia and mercenaries within the imperial army was consolidated, and the Argonautic tale of seeking the Golden Fleece was systematised by Greek writers over the following two or three centuries. In the long run the empire nailed this Caucasus–Black Sea frontier in place, but it preserved the local Greek colouring, the Greek commerce and the residue of the local monarchy, which is why a kingdom of Colchis still existed when the Romans took over.
result: 就軍事層面而言，這場戰爭以帝國取得對黑海東岸的宗主權告終：科爾基斯本地王權被降為帝國框架內的統治者，必須繳納貢賦、供應役夫與兵員，御道驛站把這一帶接入薩迪斯到蘇薩的通訊網，沿海據點則成為帝國向黑海與北高加索推進的跳板。戰役的過程本身沒有留下逐日敘述，攻城與野戰的細節、雙方死傷人數都不可考，甚至連最後一場決戰的地點也沒有定論；可以確定的是，帝國沒有像對待某些邊疆那樣把科爾基斯王國徹底拆散，而是保留其既有結構，讓它以附庸的形式繼續存在，這是阿契美尼德治下的常見做法。技術面上，這場戰爭標誌著希臘式矛兵（dory 配 aspis）與帝國式多兵種混成軍的正面交鋒：長矛方陣在正面提供的是站得住的硬度，弓陣、戰車與重騎提供的是節奏與衝力，而防禦方的森林與河流決定了攻城與攻野的比例。最後需要說明的是，公元前560年前後這個年代，是後世編年把這場衝突繫於達里一世早期高加索經營時的慣用標記；學界對確切年份與是否只有一次大規模戰役仍有討論，比較穩健的說法是：科爾基斯在整個公元前六世紀逐步被納入帝國網絡，戰爭是這個漸進過程中的一段。
resultEn: On the military level the war ended with imperial suzerainty over the eastern Black Sea: the Colchian monarchy was reduced to a ruler inside the imperial frame, paying tribute and supplying forced labour and troops, while the relay stations of the Royal Road tied the region into the Sardis–Susa communications network and the coastal bases became springboards for further imperial movement toward the Black Sea and the northern Caucasus. The course of the fighting survives in no day-by-day narrative: the details of siege and field combat and the losses on both sides are beyond recovery, and even the site of the last decisive action is not settled. What can be said is that the empire did not dissolve the Colchian kingdom as it did with some other border polities, but kept its existing structure and let it survive in dependent form, which was the usual Achaemenid practice. Technically the war marks a head-on meeting of Greek spearmen (dory with aspis) and the imperial multi-branch combined-arms army: the hoplite block contributed hardness on the front, the archers, chariots and heavy cavalry contributed tempo and shock, and the defenders' forest and rivers decided the balance between siege and manoeuvre. One caveat must be stated: the date around 560 BC is the conventional label later chronologies attach to this clash when they place it in Darius I's early Caucasian work, and scholars still debate the exact year and whether there was a single large campaign. The steadier statement is that Colchis was drawn progressively into the imperial network across the whole sixth century BC, and that this war is one episode in that gradual process.
